709644.t: Genitive singular of ὁμός (homós, “same”), used adverbially.

709682.t: Traditionally derived as a u-stem o-grade adjective of Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱ- (“sharp”) and compared with ὄκρις (ókrĭs, “point, prominence”); however, such a stem and ablaut combination is rather strange.

709667.t: PIE word *h₁nómn̥ From ὄνομα (ónomă, “name”) + -άζω (-ázō, denominative verb suffix).

709659.t: Derived from the root of ὄναρ (ónăr) with a suffix *-yos.Cognate with Old Armenian անուրջ (anurǰ) and Albanian ëndërr.

709650.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₃m̥bʰ-l̥- (“navel”), from *h₃nebʰ- (“navel, center”). Cognates include Sanskrit नभ्य (nábhya), Latin umbilīcus, and Old English nafola (English navel).

709611.t: Traditionally connected to Sanskrit अभ्र (abhrá), Latin imber, and Old Armenian ամբ (amb), but formal derivation from Proto-Indo-European *n̥bʰrós presents several problems. *n̥, *bʰ would be expected to yield α, φ (ă, ph), although Miller's law would…

709602.t: Possibly from *Holbʰ- 'cry, lament'. Compare ὀλολύζω (ololúzō), ὀλολυγμός (ololugmós).

709698.t: From ὅπλον (hóplon, “tool, arms”). Compare typologically the relation of Russian копы́то (kopýto), копьё (kopʹjó).

709699.t: From ὅπλον (hóplon, “instrument of war; arms or armour”) + -ίτης (-ī́tēs).

709631.t: From ὁμοιόω (homoióō, “to make like, to be like”) + -σις (-sĭs).

709632.t: From ὁμόλογος (homólogos, “in agreement”), from ὁμός (homós, “same”) + λόγος (lógos, “reasoning”), + -έω (-éō, denominative verbal suffix).

709697.t: The usual explanation is to regard the base *ὀπί- (*opĭ́-) < Proto-Hellenic *opí, *opi- < Proto-Indo-European *h₁opi, as an ablaut variant of ἐπί (epĭ́, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁epi).

709669.t: PIE word *h₁nómn̥ From ὀνομάζω (onomázō, “I name”) + -τός (-tós, verbal adjective suffix).

709616.t: From Proto-Hellenic *ókʷmə (“look, glance”), from the radical *ὀπ- (from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ekʷ- (“eye”)) + -μα (-ma), with regressive assimilation (compare the Aeolic form ὄππα (óppă), with progressive assimilation).

709614.t: From ὅμιλος (hómīlos, “a crowd or gathering of people”) + -ία (-ĭ́ā).

709658.t: From Proto-Hellenic *oneidos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃neyd-os (“blame, revilement”); compare Gothic 𐌽𐌴𐌹𐌸 (neiþ), Sanskrit निन्दा (nindā́), Latvian naids.

709652.t: From ὁμῶς (homôs, “together; equally, alike”), with stress shift.

709605.t: Beekes suggests a Pre-Greek origin, compare likely cognate Old Armenian ոլոռն (oloṙn); for more see Arabic خُلَّر (ḵullar).

709612.t: Probably a compound of ὁμοῦ (homoû, “together”) + the ἀρ- (ăr-) found in ἀραρίσκω (ărărĭ́skō, “to fasten; to join”), i.e. "joined together" > "one who is forced to accompany" > "pledge, hostage".

709688.t: From the radical *ὀπ- (from Proto-Indo-European *h₃ekʷ-), the same root of ὄμμα (ómma, “eye”).

709604.t: A technical Pre-Greek word, with suffix in -νθ-.

709651.t: It could derive from Proto-Indo-European *h₃nebʰ- (“navel”), but the semantic explanation as a navel-like knob is hardly convincing. Furnée connects ἀμφίας (amphías, “bad Sicilian wine”) and ἀμφής (amphḗs, “wine blossom”).

709678.t: From ὀξύς (oxús, “sharp; sour”), with an analogous formation as ἦδος (êdos, “delight, pleasure”) to ἡδύς (hēdús, “pleasant, sweet”).

709653.t: Etymology tree Pre-Greekbor.? Ancient Greek ὄνος (ónos) Proto-Indo-European *h₂eǵ-? Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵros Proto-Indo-European *-yós Proto-Indo-European *h₂éǵr̥yos Ancient Greek ἄγριος (ắgrĭos) Ancient Greek ὄναγρος From ὄνος (ónos, “ass, donkey”)…

709662.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₃n̥-né-h₂-ti, from the root *h₃neh₂- (“to enjoy”). Cognate with Proto-Germanic *unnaną.

709689.t: From relative ὅς (hós) (or from its stem) + πηνίκα (pēníka). Compare ἡνίκα (hēníka).
